subject: Security intake: audit schema questions and SSO edge-case triage
messages:
From: Danielle Harper <d.harper@clientcorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: cloudops@acmehealth.io, compliance@medihealth.com
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Request: audit event schema + short-term retention option

Hi Sofia,

We ran a brief intake with our security team and need two things clarified before we sign the pilot PO: (1) a copy of the server-side audit event schema (fields, max sizes, and which events are persisted by default) and (2) whether Redwood can support a 30-day retention tier for a scoped dataset (audit only) while the rest of our data remains at the standard 365-day window.

The attached intake form has the details we captured. Specific asks: example event for SSO/auth flows (including device_id, idp_assertion_id, and session_cookie_id), how we can request exports via API, and what the cost profile looks like for a short retention window plus retrieval.

Can you loop in the product/infra folks and let us know the earliest we can get a schema export and a proposed implementation path?

Thanks,
Danielle
Senior IT Compliance
ClientCorp (on behalf of MediHealth)

Attachments: medihealth-intake-form.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Harper <d.harper@clientcorp.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com, tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit event schema + short-term retention option

Danielle — thanks for the note and the intake form. Looping in Product (Grace), Ops (Tessa), and Infra (Priyom) to triage.

Initial notes:
- We can export a draft audit schema by EOD Weds, but there are open fields (payload blobs, optional PII tags) we need to annotate before sharing.
- A scoped 30-day audit retention tier is feasible technically (ephemeral-index + shorter TTL), but it has product and billing implications we should surface: sampling vs full retention, export speed, and SLA on retrieval.

Grace / Priyom / Tessa — can you each confirm: (A) which schema fields are considered PHI/PII and must be redacted by default, (B) whether a 30-day TTL for an audit-only stream requires a separate index or can be layered via metadata TTL, and (C) estimated uplift in monthly cost for retrievals >30 days (ballpark). I will consolidate and send MediHealth a short plan.

Sofia
Product Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit event schema + short-term retention option

Sofia — quick product take and attached draft schema (audit-schema-v1.xlsx). Highlights:
- Core event fields we always persist: timestamp, org_id, project_id, request_id, model_id, action, actor_type, actor_id (hashed), status_code.
- SSO/auth flows: we currently store idp_name, idp_event_type, token_thumbprint (SHA256), and a blob for idp_assertion (configurable to truncate). We do not persist raw idp assertions by default.
- PII: device_id and client-provided user_email are optional fields; by default we hash device_id and drop user_email unless the customer opts into enhanced telemetry.

Regarding retention approach:
- Option A (fast): metadata-TTL layered on same index; cheaper to implement but makes retrieval slightly slower for archived events.
- Option B (clean): separate ephemeral index for 30-day audits; better retrieval guarantees and simpler compliance scoping but increases operational overhead and cost.

Ballpark uplift: Option A ~ +8–12% on audit storage costs; Option B ~ +18–30% depending on query frequency. Precise estimates need workload profile.

Next steps: Priyom to confirm infra feasibility for separate index and any I/O constraints; Tessa to propose a short retrieval SLA for archived 30-day exports. I can prepare a short customer-facing summary for MediHealth once we have infra numbers.

—Grace
PM, Security & Compliance

Attachments: audit-schema-v1.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit event schema + short-term retention option

TL;DR: infra can do both Option A and B, with implementation windows and infra caveats below.

Feasibility notes:
- Option A (metadata TTL): short rollout (1–2 sprints) — update retention controller to respect event-level retention metadata; no new indices required; retrieval via existing export path (slower for older segments).
- Option B (separate ephemeral index): medium rollout (3–5 sprints) — requires index lifecycle policies, cross-cluster replication checks for Dedicated, and changes to the query router so RBAC and scoped queries hit the ephemeral indexes first.
- SSO edge-case: idp_assertion_id and session_cookie_id are stored in the KV cache for session routing currently; we do not persist raw assertion blobs in hot storage by default. If MediHealth requires assertion persistence, we need explicit opt-in and field-level retention controls. That is an additional compliance gating item and will require a legal sign-off.

Cost/ops: Option A will be cheaper but will complicate audit granularity (harder to isolate entirely); Option B gives cleaner compliance boundaries. Retrieval SLA proposal for archived 30-day exports: 48 hours for a full dataset export (can be improved for a premium SLA).

I'll scope work items into SUP-4332 and estimate story points by EOD Friday.

Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Danielle Harper <d.harper@clientcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit event schema + short-term retention option

Danielle — thanks for the intake. Per the triage above: we can deliver a customer-facing summary and an implementation plan by next Wednesday that lists the two retention options, cost buckets, and the retrieval SLA. Grace attached the draft schema; if MediHealth wants assertion persistence (idp_assertion), that will be listed as an exception and require legal & product approval.

Action items:
- Danielle: confirm whether MediHealth wants device_id hashed (default) or raw (requires exception).
- Danielle: confirm target query cadence for archived exports (ad-hoc vs weekly scheduled) so we can refine cost.
- Sofia: please raise SUP-4332 and include the intake form + audit-schema-v1.xlsx (Priyom will add infra story points).

I'll follow up with the customer-facing plan and cc legal if they ask for assertion persistence.

Thanks,
Tessa
Security Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
